title: The International Court of Justice and the Judicial Settlement of Disputes

excerpt: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations and the central forum for the judicial settlement of disputes between states. This article explains the Court’s Charter foundation, contentious jurisdiction, advisory jurisdiction, provisional measures, preliminary objections, evidentiary practice, judgments, compliance, and doctrinal influence across state responsibility, self-determination, territorial disputes, maritime delimitation, use of force, genocide, occupation, and the legal consequences of unlawful situations.
